podcast.body: This song was written in 1993 while Radiohead was on tour with James. It was later released as the lead track of an EP, which, depending on the version, might have included up to eight new songs. The band road-tested the song live in Toronto on June 6, 1995. The title refers to a massive medical machine used to assist breathing, and Tom York reportedly owns a real one at home. "It's called My Iron One."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released as a single significantly before *The Bends*, "My Iron Lung" served as a warm-up to gauge market reaction to Radiohead's evolving musical direction. While initially released as a normal single worldwide, an Australian EP version, featuring an acoustic version of "Creep" and eight songs, was later created. This EP's success led to its subsequent re-fabrication and distribution across the rest of the world, though its origin and initial global distribution timeline were distinct from the album. "Si es verdad que Mayeron Lang salió como single antes del disco, bastante antes del disco como calendamiento para ver cómo reaccionaba, un poco el mercado al pequeño cambio de tendencia que había hecho radioje."

podcast.body: This single or EP was released considerably before the final *The Bends* album, as a result of EMI's doubts and pressure for hits. Its initial reception was "no era especialmente buena."
